review.summary: Reviewed the first-parent diff, Joolia’s pre-batch code, and the resulting merged tree. This is a behavior-preserving refactor of binding-write diagnostics; no zero-origin adaptation or test edit is needed.

commits.subsystems: Native module/binding-partition runtime in src/module.c:910-946; callers in src/builtins.c:1522-1557, src/interpreter.c:750-757, and src/codegen.cpp:3845-3858. The refactor also relies on the shared partition-kind definitions in src/julia.h, src/julia_internal.h, and base/runtime_internals.jl.
commits.indexing_implications: No collection position, dimension, count, byte offset, or zero-origin conversion is involved. The numeric PARTITION_KIND_* values are internal enum/tag encodings read by jl_binding_kind and classified by jl_bkind_is_some_global, jl_bkind_is_some_guard, and jl_bkind_is_some_constant; they are identifiers/state tags, not indexes or sentinels, so their values must remain unchanged. The Joolia definitions preserve the upstream global predicate exactly: only PARTITION_KIND_GLOBAL and PARTITION_KIND_DECLARED are writable. Existing guard, constant, and import consumers were inspected, including the C-side distinction where UNDEF_CONST is handled by the constant branch.
commits.adaptations: None. Upstream moves the existing guard/constant/import diagnostics from jl_check_binding_currently_writable into jl_binding_not_writable_error, adds an assertion that the helper receives neither writable kind, and replaces !jl_bkind_is_some_global(kind) with the equivalent explicit comparison. Joolia’s predicate and enum contracts are unchanged, and the resulting helper preserves the same error text, module lookup through jl_binding_dbgmodule, noreturn annotation, and safepoint annotation. No origin conversion is justified.
commits.tests: Recommended, not executed: rebuild the runtime, run make -C src analyze-module -j8, and run the affected rebinding coverage in test/rebinding.jl, especially PartitionImportTarget stores at lines 699-712, StaleStoreTarget guard failures at lines 773-783, and the compiled imported-store path in Compiler/test/inference.jl:7951. Then run the required gate python3 contrib/ci/run.py --jobs 4. These checks should confirm writable GLOBAL/DECLARED partitions remain writable and GUARD, CONSTANT, and imported partitions retain their existing diagnostics.
